tweets.title: MASSIVE CRACK DOWN ON PAKISTANI ISI-BACKED TERROR NETWORK Union Home Minister Amit Shah said security agencies arrested 200+ operatives linked to the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day. According to the government, coordinated operations across 14 states led to the recovery of IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, firearms and surveillance equipment. ThePrint, citing PTI and a government statement, reported that the network was allegedly involved in grenade, IED and petrol-bomb attacks, targeted killings and reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites. tweets.content:
MASSIVE CRACK DOWN ON PAKISTANI ISI-BACKED TERROR NETWORK

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said security agencies arrested 200+ operatives linked to the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day.

According to the government, coordinated operations across 14 states led to the recovery of IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, firearms and surveillance equipment.

ThePrint, citing PTI and a government statement, reported that the network was allegedly involved in grenade, IED and petrol-bomb attacks, targeted killings and reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites.

Over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests have been recorded against the network under UAPA and other laws.

Source: ThePrint/PTI

tweets.content:
Breaking: India arrests over 200 operatives in multi-state crackdown on ISI-linked Shahzad Bhatti terror network; recovered arms and explosives ahead of Independence Day, annouces India's Home Minister Amit Shah

Amit Shah (@AmitShah)

Modi govt destroyed the ISI-backed terror group Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day and thwarted its plans for subversive attacks by arresting more than 200 operatives.

Indian security forces ripped apart the network by launching coordinated operations across different locations in 14 states upholding a brilliant example of India's zero-tolerance towards terrorism.

Substantial recoveries, including IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, live cartridges, and CCTV cameras used for espionage, were made from the ISI-funded group. The network was involved in several terrorist activities.

tweets.title: US WITHDRAWS ITS LAST AIRCRAFT CARRIER FROM INDO-PACIFIC The US has temporarily withdrawn its last forward-deployed aircraft carrier from the Western Pacific, with USS George Washington heading to West Asia to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln. The redeployment highlights mounting pressure on the US Navy’s 11-carrier fleet as Washington balances military commitments in West Asia with the growing Chinese challenge in the Indo-Pacific. With no US carrier currently forward-deployed in the Western Pacific, concerns are growing over the impact on US power projection and deterrence around Taiwan and the South China Sea.
tweets.content:
US WITHDRAWS ITS LAST AIRCRAFT CARRIER FROM INDO-PACIFIC

The US has temporarily withdrawn its last forward-deployed aircraft carrier from the Western Pacific, with USS George Washington heading to West Asia to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln.

The redeployment highlights mounting pressure on the US Navy’s 11-carrier fleet as Washington balances military commitments in West Asia with the growing Chinese challenge in the Indo-Pacific.

With no US carrier currently forward-deployed in the Western Pacific, concerns are growing over the impact on US power projection and deterrence around Taiwan and the South China Sea.

tweets.title: Army Chief Dhiraj Seth visits Nepal to strengthen military ties Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth is on a three-day visit to Nepal from August 17–19 to further strengthen defence cooperation and military-to-military ties. A key highlight will be Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel conferring upon Gen Seth the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army, a unique tradition shared by the two armies. Gen Seth will also meet Nepal’s military leadership, discuss issues of mutual interest, address student officers at the Army Command and Staff Course, and interact with Indian Army veterans in Pokhara.
tweets.content:
Army Chief Dhiraj Seth visits Nepal to strengthen military ties

Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth is on a three-day visit to Nepal from August 17–19 to further strengthen defence cooperation and military-to-military ties.

A key highlight will be Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel conferring upon Gen Seth the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army, a unique tradition shared by the two armies.

Gen Seth will also meet Nepal’s military leadership, discuss issues of mutual interest, address student officers at the Army Command and Staff Course, and interact with Indian Army veterans in Pokhara.

tweets.title: Trump’s demands stretch US Navy to its limits The US Navy is facing mounting pressure as Trump pushes an ambitious fleet expansion while existing forces remain stretched by prolonged deployments, shipbuilding delays and rising costs. The USS Abraham Lincoln spent a record 260 days at sea without a port visit, surpassing the previous 204-day record. Sailors and families have raised concerns over exhaustion and mental health. At the same time, Trump’s proposed “Golden Fleet” includes nuclear-powered battleships potentially costing over $23 billion each, while US shipyards are already struggling with backlogs involving carriers, submarines and destroyers. The administration is also reviewing a return to steam-powered catapults on Ford-class carriers, potentially disrupting the electromagnetic launch systems already being developed.
tweets.content:
Trump’s demands stretch US Navy to its limits

The US Navy is facing mounting pressure as Trump pushes an ambitious fleet expansion while existing forces remain stretched by prolonged deployments, shipbuilding delays and rising costs.

The USS Abraham Lincoln spent a record 260 days at sea without a port visit, surpassing the previous 204-day record. Sailors and families have raised concerns over exhaustion and mental health.

At the same time, Trump’s proposed “Golden Fleet” includes nuclear-powered battleships potentially costing over $23 billion each, while US shipyards are already struggling with backlogs involving carriers, submarines and destroyers.

The administration is also reviewing a return to steam-powered catapults on Ford-class carriers, potentially disrupting the electromagnetic launch systems already being developed.
